Combining Boolean conditions

Unit 1 · Week 3 · Lesson 2 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Python editor, paper response cards and a four-row truth-table frame.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Combining Boolean conditions

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Success: explain and/or/not, evaluate a combined rule and use parentheses to make grouping explicit. Use supplied Boolean values rather than parsing yes/no input.

2. Retrieval: the equality boundary

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual retrieval with correction

Expected False, True and True. Ask for one minute of individual work, then paired explanations. If > and >= remain confused, return to the number-line boundary before combining conditions.

3. Both, either and the opposite

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked truth table

Model the first row and ask learners to predict the remaining rows before revealing them or checking with Python. and requires both True, or needs at least one True and includes both, not reverses a Boolean. Here P and Q stand for Boolean values. A common error is interpreting or as exactly one.

4. An eligibility rule

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher modelling and paired variation

Rule: eligibility requires age at least 16 AND permission. With supplied values age 16 and has_permission False, result is False. Ask learners to predict changing permission to True, then age to 15. Expected True then False. has_permission is already bool. bool("False") is True because the string is non-empty, so do not use it to parse input.

5. Grouping changes which rule you test

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided prediction and peer explanation

Use the stated values to evaluate both expressions. A is True because and binds more tightly than or. B is False because the parenthesised or is True but not suspended is False. Explain Python Boolean operator precedence: not, then and, then or. Comparisons here evaluate before these Boolean combinations. Ask learners to annotate sub-results. If confusion remains, replace each sub-expression with True/False on paper.

6. Testing every Boolean combination

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Paired investigation with role changes

Use supplied booleans rather than text input. Learners implement allowed = (member or guest) and not suspended and choose cases before running. Expected True/False/False gives True; False/True/False gives True; True/True/True gives False; False/False/False gives False. These cover key paths but not all eight combinations. Stretch: test all eight and justify coverage. Support: add intermediate (member or guest) results.

7. What does or allow?

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: All-student misconception check

Collect responses before discussion. Correct B: True or True is True. Explain inclusive or allows both. If learners choose A, use the truth-table first row and recheck True or False. Ask them to contrast and, which requires both.

8. Exit ticket: a combined decision

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent exit ticket

Rule: both age >= 16 and has_permission, reversed permission with not. Expected age 16/permission False gives False for eligibility, age 15/permission True gives False and age 16/permission True gives True. not False is True. Collect without Python first. Group follow-up support by comparison, conjunction or negation errors.
